title: Wavelets, whitening, activations and an audit: transforms you choose or learn, and the checks they need
summary: These course animations cover transforms that depend on data or are learned: a sparse wavelet approximation, whitening by PCA, one network layer deforming a grid, and an audit that re-derives the equation a transformed variable must obey. Companion static figures show a wavelet scale map, the three stages of whitening, six activation functions with their derivatives, and two coordinate transforms with their field derivatives.

media.alt: A scatter of correlated points inside an orange covariance ellipse with printed eigenvalues, condition number and mean; the group also has a wavelet reconstruction against the true signal, three deformed grids for three activation functions coloured by the determinant of the Jacobian, and a four-panel audit of raw and transformed decay with the induced field.

read_the_figure.question: What does this transform change about the data or the equation, and which printed number confirms it did so correctly?
read_the_figure.axes: S016: feature 1 against feature 2 with a stage readout (stage p = 1.01). S015: signal against position, and L2 error against number of kept coefficients on log axes. S017: the plane, each panel a grid mapped by one layer; colour is log10 |det J|. S018: time, state, transformed state z and the induced field g(z).
look_at: S016: the ellipse is the covariance; its axes are the eigenvectors. The text lists the eigenvalues (0.27 and 4.00), the condition number (14.62) and the mean (about zero). After whitening the ellipse should be a circle and the condition number 1.

S015: the grey curve is the signal, the blue the reconstruction from K = 27 of 256 Haar coefficients (error 2.458). The error curve falls steeply and drops to nearly zero once enough coefficients are kept.
S017: three panels, ReLU, tanh and softplus. Dark colour means the layer has squashed the area (small determinant); the titles report the smallest |det J| over the grid, about 0.97, 0.99 and 1.1.

S018: the left two panels are the raw state y(t) and the transformed z(t) for two candidate transforms (log(y + d) and asinh(y/d)); the lower panels are the raw field f(y) and the induced field g(z). The small text gives the audit residual, about 4e-12 and 7e-12.

Companion figures. Wavelet scale map: a two-bump signal (narrow bump at 0.45, wide one at 0.75) and its scale-time map; the narrow bump lights up at small scales and the wide one at larger scales, with a dashed cone where edge effects matter.
Whitening geometry: three panels show centred correlated features, the PCA-rotated cloud (axes aligned with the coordinate axes, unequal spread) and the whitened scores (a round cloud).

Activation functions and derivatives: ReLU, leaky ReLU, softplus, tanh, SiLU and GELU, each with its derivative as a dashed curve; ReLU's derivative is a step, tanh's derivative peaks at one and decays to zero in both tails.

Two transformed coordinates: shifted log and asinh of a positive physical state, and the derivative of the transformed field; the shifted log has a derivative of about -21 near y = 0 while asinh stays near -10.
read_the_figure.proves: S016 proves a linear change of variables removed correlation and set the scale of every direction. S015 shows how few coefficients carry the signal in a good basis. S017 shows how much area a layer destroys. S018 proves, by a residual at round-off size, that the equation for the transformed variable was derived correctly.
if_wrong: A condition number far above 1 after whitening: the covariance was estimated from too few samples or the data are nearly degenerate.
An error curve that decays slowly with K: the basis does not fit the signal (here a chirp at high position is expensive for Haar functions).
Dark areas in the activation grid: a layer collapses regions, so an inverse (or a change-of-variables density) fails there.
An audit residual well above round-off: the transformed ODE is not equivalent to the raw one, and a model trained on z learns the wrong dynamics.
must_check: That the covariance used for whitening is computed on training data only.
That the number of kept coefficients and the error norm are both stated.
That the colour scale of a determinant map is logarithmic and labelled.
That the audit compares the induced field with a numerical derivative of the transformed trajectory.

terms.meaning: A linear map that gives data zero mean and identity covariance.
Ratio of its largest to smallest eigenvalue. Large means some directions are much more variable than others.
A basis of piecewise-constant steps at several scales. Orthonormal, so errors are sums of squared coefficients.
Keep the K largest coefficients and set the rest to zero.
A fixed nonlinear map applied to each unit of a layer: ReLU, tanh, softplus.
The right-hand side that the transformed variable obeys: g(z) = Phi'(y) f(y).

remember: After whitening, covariance is the identity and the condition number is 1.
For an orthonormal basis, the squared L2 error of a K-term approximation is the sum of the squared dropped coefficients; keeping the largest K is optimal.
The Jacobian determinant of a layer is det W times the product of the activation slopes.
A transformed ODE is dz/dt = Phi'(y) f(y) with y written in terms of z.
An audit residual near 1e-12 means 'equal'; 1e-3 means a mistake.

steps.title: Whitening by eigen-decomposition
steps.note: Rotate to the eigenvectors (the ellipse axes), then divide each coordinate by the square root of its eigenvalue. The ellipse becomes a circle and the condition number falls from 14.6 to 1.

steps.title: Why keeping the largest coefficients is optimal
steps.note: Parseval's identity: the error is the energy in the discarded coefficients. Discarding the smallest ones loses least energy, which is why the error curve falls monotonically with K.

steps.title: Jacobian of one layer
steps.note: ReLU has slope 0 or 1, so one inactive unit gives det J = 0 (a collapsed region, dark in the picture). tanh and softplus have slopes in (0, 1] and (0, 1): never exactly zero but small where saturated.

steps.title: The induced field by the chain rule
steps.note: For z = log(y + d) this reads g = f/(y + d). The audit differentiates the transformed trajectory numerically and compares it with g(z).

steps.title: What the audit residual measures
steps.note: If r is at round-off size the two descriptions are the same system. Anything larger means the transform, the field or the derivative was written wrongly.

steps.title: Derivatives of the common activations
steps.note: The companion figure plots each function with its derivative; the derivative is what multiplies the backward signal, so tails with derivative near zero (tanh) and exact zeros (ReLU for x below 0) are where gradients vanish.

worked.title: Condition number before and after whitening
worked.problem: The still prints covariance eigenvalues 0.27 and 4.00. Compute the condition number, and the eigenvalues after whitening.

solution.text: After whitening every eigenvalue is one.

worked.answer: About 14.8 (the screen shows 14.62 because the printed eigenvalues are rounded), reduced to exactly 1.

analyze.q: Why can whitening make an optimizer's life easier, and why can it hurt when the smallest eigenvalue is noise?
analyze.hint: Dividing by sqrt(lambda) multiplies noise directions.

analyze.q: In the activation grid, which of the three panels could have an exactly zero determinant at some point, and what would that do to a normalizing flow built from it?
analyze.hint: Look at the slope of ReLU.

analyze.q: Two transforms, log(y + d) and asinh(y/d), give different induced fields. What can you tell from the shape of g(z) about how stiff each makes the problem?
analyze.hint: Steep g means a fast clock.

evaluate.q: Is a wavelet basis a good choice for this signal? Use the error against K to argue.
evaluate.hint: Compare with how few coefficients a smooth signal would need.

evaluate.q: The audit passes at 1e-12. List two things it does not guarantee about a transform.
evaluate.hint: Invertibility over the whole data range; conditioning.

create: Write a three-line audit for any new transform of a state variable and decide which number goes in the figure title.
Design a figure that shows how much area each layer of a small network collapses, using a colour scale that stays readable over six decades.

checks.q: What does the ellipse axes in the whitening still represent?
checks.hint: Eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the covariance.
checks.answer: The directions of largest and smallest variance (eigenvectors) with lengths proportional to the square root of the eigenvalues.

checks.q: Eigenvalues 9 and 1: condition number before and standard deviation scale factors for whitening?
checks.answer: Condition number 9; whitening divides the first direction by 3 and the second by 1.

checks.q: Why does the L2 error curve drop to nearly zero near K of about 120 out of 256?
checks.answer: The signal has only about that many nonzero Haar coefficients (it is piecewise constant over part of the interval), so keeping them all reproduces it exactly.

checks.q: Is a transform that passes an audit at 1e-12 safe to train on?
checks.answer: Not necessarily. It shows the equations are equivalent, but not that the map is invertible over the data range or well conditioned; those need separate checks.

checks.q: Propose a title for the activation-grid figure that makes collapse easy to see.
checks.hint: Print the smallest determinant and the dead fraction.
checks.answer: For example 'ReLU: min |det J| = 0.97, 0 percent of grid cells collapsed', so a reader can compare layers numerically as well as by colour.
